title: 第二十九章 淬迹
content_zh:
旧库房后的阴影，成了陈默专属的、弥漫着锈味、尘土和紧张气息的“工坊”。

    他将那包沉重的油布包裹藏在库房墙角一个半塌的、用来堆放废弃陶瓮的破木架下，用几块破烂的草席和朽木仔细掩盖好。接下来的几天，他像一只谨慎的、在猎食者领地边缘活动的鼹鼠，只在夜深人静、确认杂役院彻底陷入沉睡后，才会悄无声息地溜出通铺，来到此处。

    夜风寒凉刺骨，但他浑然不觉。他的全部心神，都系在眼前这几件锈迹斑斑的金属物件上。

    他没有立刻去动那几块沉甸甸的黑纹铁锭。那东西太显眼，处理起来动静也大，暂时不是他能染指的。他的目标，是那几件小巧的工具——弯钩、凿杆、薄片。

    工具入手冰凉，表面覆盖着暗红、棕褐、墨绿混杂的厚厚锈层，有些地方锈蚀得已经与本体难分彼此，散发出浓郁的、令人胸口发闷的铁腥和土腥气。他尝试用手指抠、用柴刀背刮，收效甚微，锈层坚硬如石，稍一用力，便有簌簌的锈粉落下，呛人口鼻。

    直接硬来不行。他需要“温和”地去除锈蚀，又不能损伤底下可能已经脆弱的金属本体。

    他想到了苏芸传授的草药知识。某些草药汁液，因其酸性或特殊成分，可用于清除金属表面污垢、锈迹，甚至辅助某些矿石的初步处理。周安笔记上，也有类似记载，但语焉不详。

    他仔细回忆。苏芸提过，“酸浆草”捣烂取汁，有微弱的腐蚀性，可清洁某些器皿。“乌柏叶”煮水，性涩，常用于浸泡生锈的农具，可软化锈层。还有“明矾”，虽非草药，但其性收敛、澄清，与某些酸性汁液混合，据说能增强去污除锈之效，但需注意用量，过量反易损伤器物。

    这些东西，杂役院里或后山外围，或许能找到。

    于是，白天砍柴、劳作之余，陈默开始“不务正业”。他利用一切机会，目光如同最细致的篦子，扫过途经的每一寸土地，每一丛杂草。砍柴时，他会“顺便”采集几株叶片肥厚、边缘呈锯齿状的酸浆草，用破布包好塞进怀里。清理水沟时，他会留意岸边是否有叶片宽大、呈卵形的乌柏树幼苗，偷偷摘下几片嫩叶。他甚至趁去灶房后倒垃圾时，在堆放煤渣和炉灰的角落，用柴刀尖小心地拨弄，寻找可能残留的、未完全燃烧的、含有明矾成分的矿石碎屑（某些廉价引火矿石中偶有掺杂）。

    他像个最吝啬的守财奴，一点点地积攒着这些微不足道的、旁人视为垃圾的“材料”。动作隐蔽，神色如常，绝不多拿，也绝不在同一处停留过久。酸浆草汁液需要捣烂过滤，他就用一块捡来的、相对平整的石片和一根木棍，在夜深人静时，于库房后的角落里，极其轻微地捣碾，然后将浑浊的汁液用破布过滤到一个小瓦片中。乌柏叶则被他揉碎，泡在另一个破陶碗的清水中。找到的明矾碎屑，也被他小心地碾成粉末，用一小片干树叶包好。

    材料备齐，他开始了第一次尝试。

    他选择了那件最小的、形似柳叶的弧形薄片工具。这工具锈蚀相对较轻，形状也最简单。他用一根细木棍，小心地蘸取少许酸浆草汁液，涂抹在薄片工具一端的锈层上。汁液呈淡绿色，带着刺鼻的酸气。涂抹上去，起初并无反应。等了约莫半盏茶时间，借着远处主峰投来的、极其微弱的光线，陈默隐约看到，涂抹处的锈层颜色似乎变深了些，表面也微微湿润、软化。

    他不敢怠慢，立刻用另一根缠了少许破布的木棍，蘸取泡了乌柏叶的浑浊水，轻轻擦拭涂抹过酸浆草汁液的地方。乌柏叶水颜色暗黄，带着一股草木的涩味。两相接触，被酸浆草软化了的锈层，竟真的被擦下了一些暗红色的、黏腻的糊状物！

    有效！陈默心中一喜，但手上动作更加轻柔缓慢。他深知，这工具锈蚀日久，金属本体可能也已脆弱不堪，用力稍猛，或许就会连同锈层一起，将工具本身擦断或刮出凹痕。

    他耐心地，蘸取一点酸浆草汁液，涂抹一小块区域，等待，再用乌柏叶水擦拭，再用干净的破布吸去污渍。如此循环，一点一点，如同在修复一件最珍贵的、却又脆弱不堪的古董。锈层顽固的地方，他会尝试加入极少量的明矾粉末，与酸浆草汁液混合后再涂抹，效果似乎更好，但刺激性也更强，散发出更刺鼻的气味，他不得不更加小心，涂抹后立刻用大量清水（取自附近一个积雨的小石坑）冲洗，防止过度腐蚀。

    这是一个极其枯燥、极其缓慢、也极其考验耐心和细心的过程。在深秋寒冷的后半夜，蹲在冰冷的墙角，对着几乎看不清的微小锈点，重复着单调的动作。手指很快被酸液和冷水浸得发白、起皱，传来刺痛。夜风如刀，穿透单薄的衣衫，带走体温，让他忍不住轻轻颤抖。左胸伤处和膻中穴的隐痛，在寒冷和长时间保持蹲姿下，也变得更加清晰。

    但他浑然忘我。全部心神都集中在指尖那一点微弱的触感，和眼前锈层那极其缓慢的变化上。他能“听”到锈层被软化、剥离时，发出的、几乎不存在的、细微的“沙沙”声；能“看”到在酸液和清水的交替作用下，暗红色的锈垢褪去，露出底下一点点、虽然依旧黯淡、却已能看出金属本色的、深沉的青黑色。

    时间，在这一次次蘸取、涂抹、等待、擦拭、冲洗的循环中，悄然流逝。当东方天际泛起第一线鱼肚白时，陈默才猛地惊醒，发现手中那件弧形薄片工具，靠近尖端约莫一寸长的部分，锈层已被基本清除干净！

    虽然只是极小的一部分，虽然露出的金属表面依旧粗糙，布满了细微的凹坑和氧化痕迹，色泽也远非光亮，但那确确实实，是工具本身的金属！是经过了不知多少岁月锈蚀掩埋后，重见天日的、属于“黑纹铁”的深沉质地！在熹微的晨光下，那一小片区域，不再是被锈垢包裹的顽石，而隐隐透出一种内敛的、沉黯的、属于精炼金属的冷硬光泽。

    更重要的是，在清除锈层的过程中，陈默对这工具的形制，有了更清晰的认知。这薄片极薄，边缘在锈层下竟隐约有开刃的痕迹，虽然此刻已被岁月磨钝，但能看出其原本的设计，绝非普通的铁片，更像是一种用于精细切割或刮削的专用刃具。

    成功了！虽然只是微不足道的一小步，但证明他的方法可行！这套来自草药知识的、粗陋的“除锈”法，配合他的耐心，真的能让这些沉寂的工具，重现一丝往昔的锋芒！

    巨大的喜悦和成就感，如同冰冷的泉水，瞬间冲刷掉一夜的疲惫和寒冷。他小心地将那件薄片工具用干净的破布包好，放回油布包裹中。又将用过的瓦片、破布、木棍等痕迹仔细清理，泼上清水，用脚将泥土踩实。然后，他迅速溜回通铺，在其他人醒来之前，躺回自己的铺位，盖上薄被，仿佛只是起夜了一趟。

    身体的疲惫和寒冷，在躺下后才如潮水般涌来，让他忍不住打了个哆嗦。手指的刺痛，胸口的隐痛，也都清晰起来。但他闭着眼睛，嘴角却几不可察地，向上弯起了一丝极淡、却无比真实的弧度。

    那是一种在无尽黑暗和压抑中，亲手凿出一线微光、并确认这光真的存在的、纯粹的快慰。

    接下来的日子，这种深夜的“劳作”，成了陈默新的、隐秘的日课。他依旧每日砍柴挑水，扮演着那个沉默、病弱、毫无威胁的杂役。但内心深处，却燃烧着一簇冰冷的、名为“探索”与“修复”的火焰。他像一只在黑暗地下默默挖掘、构筑巢穴的工蚁，不为人知，却坚定而执着。

    清除锈迹的工作，进展缓慢。他需要更多的酸浆草、乌柏叶，需要更小心地避开他人的注意，也需要在一次次失败和调整中，摸索更合适的汁液配比、涂抹时间和擦拭力度。有时酸液过浓或停留太久，会腐蚀掉本就脆弱的金属边缘，让他心疼懊恼，却也只能更加谨慎。有时锈层过于顽固，与金属本体结合紧密，用尽办法也难以剥离，他便暂时放弃，转向其他部分。
content_en:
The shadow behind the old warehouse became Chen Mo's exclusive "workshop" filled with the smell of rust, dust and tension.
He hid the heavy oilcloth package under a half-collapsed wooden shelf used to stack discarded pottery urns in the corner of the warehouse, and carefully covered it with a few tattered straw mats and rotten wood.In the next few days, he was like a cautious mole moving on the edge of a predator's territory. Only in the dead of night and after confirming that the courtyard was completely asleep, he would quietly sneak out of the main bunk and come here.
The night wind was biting and cold, but he didn't notice it.All his attention was tied to the rusty metal objects in front of him.
He did not move the heavy black-grained iron ingots immediately.That thing is too conspicuous and makes a lot of noise when handling it, so it is not within his reach for the time being.His target was those small tools - hooks, chisel rods, and flakes.
The tool is cold to the touch, and its surface is covered with a thick layer of rust that is a mixture of dark red, brown, and dark green. In some places, it is so corroded that it is indistinguishable from the main body. It emits a strong, chest-suffocating smell of iron and earth.He tried to dig with his fingers and scrape with the back of a hatchet, but with little success. The rust layer was as hard as stone. With a little force, rust powder would fall down, choking his mouth and nose.
It's not possible to do it directly.He needs to remove the rust "gently" without damaging the potentially fragile metal underneath.
He thought of the herbal knowledge taught by Su Yun.Certain herbal juices, because of their acidic or special composition, can be used to remove dirt and rust from metal surfaces, and even assist in the preliminary treatment of certain ores.There are similar records in Zhou An's notes, but the details are unclear.
He recalled carefully.Su Yun mentioned that the juice extracted from "Physalis" is slightly corrosive and can clean some utensils."Wubai leaves" are astringent when boiled in water. They are often used to soak rusty farm tools to soften the rust layer.There is also "alum", although it is not an herbal medicine, it has astringent and clarifying properties. When mixed with certain acidic juices, it is said to enhance the effect of decontamination and rust removal, but you need to pay attention to the dosage. Excessive amount may damage the utensils.
These things may be found in the courtyard or outside the back mountain.
So, while chopping firewood and working during the day, Chen Mo began to "not do his job".He took advantage of every opportunity, and his eyes were like the most meticulous grate, scanning every inch of land and every clump of weeds he passed.When cutting firewood, he would "incidentally" collect a few physalis plants with thick leaves and jagged edges, wrap them in rags and stuff them into his arms.When cleaning ditches, he would pay attention to whether there are cypress seedlings with wide, oval leaves on the shore, and secretly pluck a few young leaves.He even took out the garbage after going to the kitchen, and carefully poked at the corner where the cinders and ashes were piled up, looking for possible residual, incompletely burned ore chips containing alum (some cheap ignition ores are occasionally adulterated).
Like the stingiest miser, he accumulated bit by bit these insignificant "materials" that others regarded as rubbish.The movements are concealed, the expression is normal, never take too much, and never stay in the same place for too long.The physalis juice needs to be pounded and filtered, so he used a piece of relatively flat stone and a wooden stick that he picked up. In the dead of night, he pounded it very lightly in the corner behind the warehouse, and then filtered the turbid juice into a small tile with a rag.The black cypress leaves were crushed by him and soaked in clear water in another broken pottery bowl.He also carefully ground the alum chips he found into powder and wrapped them in a small piece of dry leaf.
With the materials ready, he started his first attempt.
He chose the smallest, thin, curved tool shaped like a willow leaf.This tool is relatively lightly rusted and has the simplest shape.Using a thin wooden stick, he carefully dipped a little physalis juice into the rust layer on one end of the thin tool.The juice is light green and has a pungent sour smell.After applying it, there was no reaction at first.After waiting for about half a cup of tea, Chen Mo could vaguely see through the extremely weak light cast by the main peak in the distance that the color of the rust layer on the smeared area seemed to have become darker, and the surface was slightly moist and softened.
He did not dare to neglect, and immediately used another wooden stick wrapped with a little rag, dipped it in the turbid water soaked in ebony leaves, and gently wiped the area where the physalis juice had been applied.The water from the cypress leaves is dark yellow in color and has a herbal astringency.When the two came into contact, some dark red, sticky paste was actually wiped off the rust layer softened by the physalis!
efficient!Chen Mo felt happy, but his hand movements were gentler and slower.He knew very well that as the tool corroded over time, the metal body might have become fragile. If he applied too much force, the tool itself might be broken or dented along with the rust layer.
He patiently dipped a little physalis juice into a small area, waited, wiped it with ebony leaf water, and then used a clean rag to absorb the stain.This cycle, bit by bit, is like restoring a most precious but fragile antique.Where the rust layer was stubborn, he would try to add a very small amount of alum powder and mix it with Physalis sap before applying it. The effect seemed better, but it was also more irritating and emitted a more pungent smell. He had to be more careful and immediately rinse it with plenty of water (taken from a small nearby rain pit) after application to prevent excessive corrosion.
This is an extremely boring, extremely slow process that also tests patience and carefulness.In the cold second half of the night in late autumn, I squatted in the cold corner, repeating monotonous movements facing the tiny rust spots that were almost invisible.The fingers soon turned white, wrinkled and stinging from the acid and cold water.The night wind was like a knife, penetrating through his thin clothes and taking away his body temperature, making him tremble slightly.The dull pain in the left chest injury and Tanzhong point also became clearer in the cold and in the squatting position for a long time.
But he forgot himself.All the attention was focused on the faint touch on the fingertips and the extremely slow change of the rust layer in front of his eyes.He could "hear" the almost non-existent, subtle "rustling" sound when the rust layer was softened and peeled off; he could "see" that under the alternating action of acid and clean water, the dark red rust scale faded away, revealing a little bit underneath. Although it was still dim, the true color of the metal, deep blue-black, could be seen.
Time passes quietly in this cycle of dipping, applying, waiting, wiping, and rinsing.When the first line of fish belly white appeared in the eastern sky, Chen Mo suddenly woke up and found that the rust layer of the curved thin tool in his hand, which was about an inch long near the tip, had been basically removed!
Although it is only a very small part, although the exposed metal surface is still rough, full of tiny pits and oxidation marks, and the color is far from bright, it is indeed the metal of the tool itself!It is the deep texture of "black grained iron" that has been exposed to the light of day after being buried by rust for countless years!Under the faint morning light, that small area was no longer a stubborn stone wrapped in rust, but faintly revealed a restrained, dark, cold and hard luster that belonged to refined metal.
More importantly, in the process of removing the rust layer, Chen Mo gained a clearer understanding of the shape of the tool.This sheet is extremely thin, and there are faint traces of sharpening on the edge under the rust layer. Although it has been blunted by time, it can be seen that its original design is not an ordinary iron sheet, but more like a special cutting tool for fine cutting or scraping.
Success!It's just a small step, but it proves that his method works!This set of crude "rust removal" methods derived from herbal knowledge, coupled with his patience, can really make these dormant tools regain a trace of their past edge!
The huge joy and sense of accomplishment, like cold spring water, instantly wash away the fatigue and coldness of the night.He carefully wrapped the thin tool in a clean rag and returned it to the oilcloth wrapper.He also carefully cleaned up traces of used tiles, rags, wooden sticks, etc., poured water on them, and trampled the soil firmly with his feet.Then, he quickly slipped back to the main bunk, lay down on his bunk before others woke up, and covered himself with a thin quilt, as if he just got up for a night trip.
The exhaustion and coldness of his body came over him like a tide after he lay down, making him shiver uncontrollably.The tingling pain in my fingers and the dull pain in my chest became clearer.But with his eyes closed, the corners of his mouth curved upward almost imperceptibly with a very faint, but extremely real arc.
It was a kind of pure joy in carving out a glimmer of light with one's own hands in the endless darkness and depression, and confirming that this light really existed.
In the following days, this late-night "labor" became Chen Mo's new and secret daily routine.He still chops wood and carries water every day, playing the role of the silent, sickly, and non-threatening handyman.But deep inside, there is a cold flame called "exploration" and "repair" burning.He is like a worker ant silently digging and building a nest in the dark underground. He is unknown, but determined and persistent.
The work of removing rust has been slow.He needs more physalis and ebony leaves, needs to be more careful to avoid the attention of others, and needs to find a more suitable juice ratio, application time and wiping intensity through repeated failures and adjustments.Sometimes the acid was too concentrated or stayed too long, which would corrode the already fragile metal edges, which made him feel distressed and annoyed, but he could only be more cautious.Sometimes the rust layer is too stubborn and is tightly bonded to the metal body, making it difficult to peel off even with all possible means, so he gives up temporarily and turns to other parts.
